prompt: City councils should make all public transport free of charge so that fewer people drive into city centres. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
text:
Nowadays many city centres is full of cars and the traffic become worse every year. Some people think that city councils should make public transport free so less people will drive. I am agree with this idea in some extent.

First of all, free buses and trains can help people to save money. Many people in my city spend a lot of money for petrol and parking, and if the bus is free they will choose it. For example, my brother drive to his office every day because the bus ticket is expensive, but if it was free he would take the bus. Also, less cars means less pollution and the air in the city will be more clean.

Secondly, free transport is good for poor people. Students and old people often don't have enough money, so they stay at home. If transport is free they can go to work, to university or visit their friends easily. This make the society more equal.

However, there are some problems. The council need a lot of money to pay for free transport and maybe they will take this money from other services like schools or hospitals. Also, if the buses are free they will be very crowded and the people who drive now will not want to use them.

In conclusion, I think that free public transport is a good idea because it save money for people and reduce the pollution, but the government must to find the money and make more buses. So I partly agree with this statement.

prompt: Some people think that older people should be cared for by their own families, while others believe that the state should provide this care. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
text:
As people live longer, societies have to decide who should look after them when they can no longer manage alone. Some argue that this is a family duty, while others believe that the state should take responsibility. In my view, the best arrangement combines both, with the state providing the professional care that families cannot.

Those who favour family care point to the emotional benefits. Older people who are looked after by their children or grandchildren usually remain in familiar surroundings and feel valued rather than forgotten. In many cultures, caring for one's parents is also seen as a natural way of repaying the care received in childhood, and it keeps generations in close contact. Moreover, family care costs the public budget very little, which matters in countries with ageing populations.

On the other hand, there are strong reasons for the state to provide this care. Many families simply lack the time, money or skills, especially when both partners work full time or live far from their parents. Conditions such as dementia require trained staff and specialised equipment that a relative cannot be expected to provide. When the whole burden falls on one family member, usually a daughter, it can damage her health, career and income.

I believe that the two views are not really opposed. Families are best placed to offer company and emotional support, whereas the state should guarantee professional medical care and help for relatives who become carers, for instance through paid leave or day centres. This way, older people receive both the attention of their family and the expertise they need.

In conclusion, although families have an important role, the state should share the responsibility so that good care does not depend on how much time or money a family has.

prompt: Many people today feel stressed by their jobs. What are the main reasons for this, and how can employers and individuals deal with it?
text:
Work-related stress has become a common problem in many countries. In this essay I will discuss the main reasons for this situation and suggest what both employers and workers can do about it.

One of the main reasons is the heavy workload. Many companies try to reduce costs, so fewer employees have to do the same amount of work, and they often stay at the office late in the evening. Another reason is technology. Because people can read e-mails on their phones, they are expected to answer messages at any time, even at weekends, and they never really rest. Finally, many workers feel insecure about their jobs, especially when the economy is weak, and this fear makes them anxious.

There are several ways to deal with this problem. Employers should make sure that the workload is realistic and hire more staff when it is necessary. They can also introduce clear rules about contacting employees after working hours. For example, some companies in Europe switch off their e-mail servers in the evening, which allow workers to disconnect completely. In addition, managers should talk regularly with their teams, so problems can be solved before they become serious.

Individuals can also take steps to protect themselves. It is important to have a healthy balance between work and free time, for instance by doing sport or spending time with family. People should also learn to say no when they are asked to do more than they can manage, and to ask for help if they feel overwhelmed.

To sum up, job stress is mainly caused by heavy workloads, constant connection and insecurity. Both companies and employees have a responsibility to reduce it, and the best results come when they work together.
